ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (creates UIAF), Ley 1121 de 2006, Ley 1357 de 2009, Ley 1762 de 2015, Ley 2010 de 2019 (Art. 631-5 ET on final beneficiaries), Decreto 830 de 2021, Circular Externa 100-000007 de 2018 of Superintendencia de Sociedades, and Circular Básica Jurídica (SARLAFT) for all AML/CFT supervised entities. Direct competent authorities: UIAF, Superintendencia de Sociedades, DIAN, and the local Chamber of Commerce for initial KYC and UBO collection.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign shareholder or corporate parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization at Colombian Consulate if the origin country is not a Hague Convention party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for incorporation proceedings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization at Colombian Consulate if required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each ultimate beneficial owner and authorized corporate representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the owner's or representative's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy then Apostille or Consular Legalization as demanded by the Colombian Chamber of Commerce

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement for paid-in capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or Consular Legalization only if expressly requested by the Colombian notary, Chamber of Commerce, or compliance counterparty; otherwise supplied as certified original

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory cross-check of all UBOs, directors, officers, and commercial counterparties against OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, UK HMT sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Colombian national restrictive lists maintained by UIAF and the Financial Information and Analysis Unit. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, PEP family member, PEP close associate, or individual appearing on any watchlist. For this low-risk standard retail grocery operation, simplified due diligence is acceptable for routine suppliers, but full enhanced due diligence is mandatory on all capital subscriptions, shareholder loans, and franchise/import supply agreements exceeding USD 10,000 per transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES – Registro Único Empresarial y Social (www.rues.org.co) and the corresponding local Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá, Cámara de Comercio de Medellín, or the chamber with territorial jurisdiction)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal corporate name must be expressed in Spanish or in a Spanish-compatible Latin-script transliteration. Non-Latin alphabets (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Cyrillic) cannot be used as the operative registered legal name; they may only appear as a secondary trade name or trademark in a separate registration. The name must begin with a distinctive descriptor, followed by the corporate acronym 'S.A.S.' where applicable, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any constituted company or reserved name in the RUES database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant has five (5) business days after formal notification to file a reconsideration motion (recurso de reposición) before the same Chamber of Commerce issuing the rejection. The Chamber must resolve within fifteen (15) business days. If the denial is confirmed, the applicant may file an appeal (recurso de apelación) before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio or the administrative authority having residual competence, within five (5) business days of the reconsideration decision. The appeal must demonstrate absence of confusing similarity, lack of conflict with restricted terminology, or material procedural error, and should annex a fresh RUES certificate showing alternative name proposals. A simultaneous new name application may be filed to avoid losing the incorporation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An S.A.S. may formally register a domicilio address for corporate service of process, but for a physical grocery retail store under ISIC 4721 and NAICS 445110, the statutory municipal operating license (uso de suelo), sanitary approval, and health inspection require a genuine physical operating site. A pure virtual office or virtual mail-forwarding address alone is not permissible as the principal registered and licensed business location. A limited virtual office can only serve as a secondary management or administrative contact, never as the regulated retail outlet.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High and quantified as approximately 70% likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 12 months of operation, attributable to mandatory health and food-safety oversight by the municipal Secretaría de Salud and periodic consumer-protection inspections by the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by the local Chamber of Commerce and Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and authentication of the private incorporation document (documento de constitución) and identity signatures
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaría Pública designated at the incorporation city
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff under Decreto-Ley 960 de 1970 and current notary fee schedules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial registration in the Registro Mercantil of the S.A.S. (merchant registration and certificate of existence)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff calculated as a percentage of capital subscribed; USD 200 is the prevailing benchmark for a low-capital retail venture

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax registration (RUT) and digital signature certificate for DIAN filings
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: DIAN (Administración de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official State fee; private integrator fees for digital certificate issuance are not included in this line item

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial UBO / Beneficiario Final report filing with the Superintendencia de Sociedades and DIAN
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No government filing fee; professional preparation fees are allocated under legal due diligence consulting

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Municipal operating license, zoning (uso de suelo) certificate, and local business registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Municipal tariff pursuant to Ley 232 de 1995 and local territorial resolution

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sanitary authorization for retail food establishment (registration with Secretaría de Salud / Invima coordination)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Territorial health fee schedule for low-risk food retail premises

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence, UBO piercing, AML/KYC policy drafting, and compliance advisory
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a low-risk retail grocery incorporation in Colombia; fixed-fee engagement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign corporate documents and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Apostille office) or Colombian Consulate in the document's origin country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille/consular fee schedule of the relevant foreign authority; estimated for up to four documents

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Articles 1-5 and 17-24; Colombian Commercial Code (Decree 410 of 1971), Articles 110, 353-357; Decree 1074 of 2015 (regulatory framework for commercial registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial competence at the principal place of domicile, under the administrative supervision of the Superintendencia de Sociedades.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución y Estatutos Sociales (or public deed, at the shareholders' election for an S.A.S.).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum legal paid-up capital for S.A.S.; the capital may be fixed freely in the bylaws. Cash contributions may be payable over a term not exceeding two years. There is no statutory escrow account requirement for S.A.S. incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [CORPORATE NAME] S.A.S. — Adopted in writing by the founding shareholder. RESOLVED: (1) The subscribed shares set forth in the incorporation instrument are fully allocated to the founding shareholder and accepted. (2) The registered office is fixed at [address], [city], Colombia, and jurisdiction is conferred on the local courts. (3) [Name] is appointed General Manager and [Name] is appointed Secretary, with statutory powers and the limitations stated in the bylaws. (4) The General Manager is authorized to register the company with the Chamber of Commerce, obtain the NIT/RUT from DIAN, open bank accounts, and execute ancillary documents. (5) All prior actions taken are ratified. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability search and preliminary clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio through MOV/RUES (Registro Único Empresarial y Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the corporate name options through the Cámara de Comercio's name availability service or in person. The authority verifies that no identical or confusingly similar registered name exists and issues the Certificado de Homonimia or non-similarity certificate.
required_dossiers: Up to three corporate name alternatives
Identification document of the requesting shareholder or legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is registered to a third party, immediately file a revised application with alternative names; no substantive cure is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and signature of the incorporation instrument and bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders (S.A.S. may be constituted by private document; optional notarization)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución and the Estatutos Sociales, including corporate purpose, capital subscription and payment schedule, shares subscribed by each shareholder, registered office, governance rules, and legal representative appointment. Execute and irrevocably adopt the instrument with all required signatures.
required_dossiers: Valid identification documents of all founding shareholders
Certificado de Homonimia or non-similarity certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any mandatory clause is omitted, amend the private document through a supplementary statement or new execution and re-present it for registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration with the Chamber of Commerce and issuance of Mercantil Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed private incorporation document and the registration forms with the Cámara de Comercio, either through the RUES portal or at the customer service window. The registry verifies formal legality, opens the Matrícula Mercantil, assigns the certificate number, and issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal.
required_dossiers: Payment receipt of applicable registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of a query or deficiency notice, correct the indicated clauses or documents within the administrative deadline and submit a corrected copy; if registration is refused, the shareholder may appeal before the Cámara de Comercio or pursue judicial review under Article 66 of CCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and legal identification registration before DIAN (NIT and RUT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN — Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Mercantil Certificate is issued, access the DIAN website and complete the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) form using the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal. Declare the main economic activity CIIU 4721, select the income tax regime and invoicing type, and obtain the NIT assignment.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Identification document of the legal representative
RUT registration form and supporting electronic data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DIAN system rejects or queries the application, review the activity codes and tax regime declarations, correct and refile; if a sanction is imposed, use the guided regularization or reconciliation procedure through the DIAN platform.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration and stamping of statutory corporate books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the corporate books required by law — shareholder register, board and shareholder meeting minutes, and accounting books — to the Cámara de Comercio for registration and stamping. This step perfects the formal corporate record-keeping obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Corporate books (Libro de Actas, Registro de Accionistas, Libro de Contabilidad)
Application for book registration and sealing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any book is rejected due to binding, numbering or format errors, correct the formal defects and submit a new application for stamping.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal or Departmental Health Secretariat (Secretaría de Salud) for sanitary authorization, together with the Curaduría Urbana for land-use and zoning compatibility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento para Establecimiento de Venta de Alimentos al por Menor (Minor Food Store Sanitary Operation Permit) and Certificado de Uso de Suelo / Urban Compatibility Certification.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) for national environmental matters, or the Regional Autonomous Corporation (CAR) / Municipal Environmental Authority where applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 — Low Environmental Impact: grocery retail does not require a Full EIA Report. The establishment must obtain an environmental registration or confirmatory environmental concept and implement mandatory solid waste and wastewater management measures.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to the public sewer must meet Resolución 0631 de 2015 thresholds: pH 6.0-9.0, TSS ≤ 175 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 90 mg/L, and COD ≤ 250 mg/L, or the limits fixed by the local sewer operator. No industrial VOC emissions threshold is applicable, but refrigeration units must comply with ozone-depleting substance handling rules under the Montreal Protocol regime. Solid waste must be segregated under Resolución 2184 de 2019 (white, black and biodegradable color code) and disposed of through the municipal collection service.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification by the Cuerpo de Bomberos; structural load and occupancy verification by the Curaduría Urbana through the applicable urban license or concept; workplace occupational health and safety (SG-SST) registration with an ARL, including employee training and risk assessment; final hygienic-sanitary clearance from the Municipal Health Secretariat after inspection.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN). Official portal: www.dian.gov.co; taxpayer electronic services platform: muisca.dian.gov.co.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Colombian S.A.S., the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) is automatically generated upon notarized incorporation and Chamber of Commerce registration. The company must complete the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) with DIAN, declaring the ISIC 4721 economic activity and VAT obligations. A foreign entity without local incorporation but engaging in taxable activities in Colombia must appoint a fiscal representative, submit apostilled powers of attorney, and apply to DIAN for a NIT via the RUT foreign-investor protocol. All procedures require a DIAN-authorized digital signature certificate (Firma Digital).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An S.A.S. is irrevocably classified as a national corporation taxable at entity level; no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch pass-through election is permitted under Colombian law. Eligible small entities may elect the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE) if annual gross income does not exceed 80,000 UVT, resulting in a unified contribution covering income tax, VAT, and municipal taxes. Otherwise, the entity remains in the standard corporate income tax and common IVA regime. No further US-style classification elections are available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre las Ventas, IVA), regulated under Decree 1625/2016 and Law 2277/2022.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Legal entities have no economic turnover threshold; every S.A.S. must register as a common-regime IVA taxpayer upon NIT assignment. For natural persons, the simplified-regime threshold is 3,500 UVT (approx. COP 148,442,000 for tax year 2023); above this threshold registration in the common regime is mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: DIAN mandates real-time electronic invoicing ('Facturación Electrónica') for all VAT taxpayers. Invoices must be transmitted through DIAN-authorized software, direct web-service API, or cloud POS with X.509 digital certificate; each invoice receives a CUFE/CUDE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) for legal clearance. Supermarket retail sales must issue an electronic sales invoice at the point of sale, validated immediately by DIAN, with QR code and CUFE printed. No post-emission digital stamping certificate is used; clearance is performed online through DIAN's computer service.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Colombian customs territory, as well as services supplied to foreign clients, may be zero-rated for IVA if the seller is an exporter registered in the RUT, the export is covered by a valid customs export declaration, and the foreign-currency proceeds are channeled through the Colombian foreign-exchange market and remitted to Colombia within statutory deadlines. For an Asian specialty grocery supermarket, zero-rating applies only to bona fide sales that physically leave Colombia and are documented as exports; local domestic sales of imported condiments remain subject to 19% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación – DEX) authorized by DIAN Customs
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical dispatch from Colombia
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Consignación de Divisas) issued by a Colombian foreign-exchange intermediary
Commercial Invoice with unit prices and commodity classification
Packing List with weights and quantities
ICA or INVIMA sanitary permits where foods or condiments are exported
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN audits export VAT refunds for up to five years and may retroactively claw back the zero-rate benefit where the foreign exchange is not repatriated within the 180-day deadline, the customs declaration is incomplete, or the goods are not actually dispatched. The taxpayer is exposed to administrative penalties of up to 200% of the improperly refunded amount, daily default interest, disqualification from refund procedures, and criminal sanctions under Law 1762 of 2015 for customs fraud and false declarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (foreign exchange administration), acting jointly with DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) for customs, validation and capital-movement control; legal framework: Régimen Cambiario (Decree 1194 of 2020, Resolution 14 of 2021 and Banco de la República regulatory circulars).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: COP is currently-account convertible for retail grocery imports and operational trade; capital-account convertibility for FDI is conditional on registration with Banco de la República through an authorized intermediary in Form No. 3 within the statutory post-receipt window (generally four months) and on the investor retaining a valid NIT and foreign-investment registration. Profit remittance is lawful when the investment registration remains valid, the S.A.S. files annual tax returns, and the remittance uses a registered profit-distribution concept; there is no blanket surrender of proceeds, but all payments and collections must pass through the formal FX channel and be documented on BDC declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For any exported goods, the S.A.S. must channel 100% of invoiced and collected foreign currency through an authorized intermediary within six months from the date of shipment; a single six-month extension may be requested from Banco de la República. The proceeds must be reported in the applicable Declaración de Cambio (Form No. 5) and either sold to the market or held in an authorized foreign-currency account. No fixed percentage peso conversion is currently operative, but the requirement is to demonstrate effective repatriation and channeling for every export operation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and FX Derivatives Clearing Eligibility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: FEASIBILITY_RATING: LOW — Colombia does not recognize European ‘EMI’ or offshore electronic-money institutions as regulated corporate banks; offshore EMIs cannot issue Colombian BDC forms, cannot maintain centralized capital accounts, and cannot serve as statutory intermediaries for the Régimen Cambiario. An authorized local fintech or payment entity may provide ancillary payment initiation but cannot replace a licensed bank for international capital injection, import settlement or FX hedging.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: REQUIRED: At least one director/legal representative and the ultimate beneficial owner must complete a physical KYC interview before the local commercial bank opens the capital escrow and operating accounts; fully remote openings are accepted only for low-risk single-owner S.A.S. entities using biometric digital onboarding, but the local manager must still appear in branch within the first operational month. Non-resident shareholders must provide notarized, apostilled resolutions and current passport plus bank-reference credentials, and the bank will validate them against SARLAFT/LAFT risk profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder domiciled in a jurisdiction considered high-risk for corruption or narcotics proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled share register, UBO declaration, source-of-funds sworn statement, three-month bank reference from the shareholder’s home financial institution, certified copies of the foreign company registration/tax identification, and a legal opinion confirming non-PEP status where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Profit margin mismatch between imported-goods master data, customs valuations and banking/payment records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sales agreements endorsed by a freight forwarder, B/L and packing list, import declaration matched against the Colombian tariff code 4721 and retail POS reports, VAT transfer invoices, and an operating inventory reconcilement signed by the S.A.S. external auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal shareholder savings or informal foreign-currency notes to fund the capital allowance without a documented investment tracing trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank transfer confirmation with SWIFT/BCR reference, investor capital contribution agreement, Form No. 3 (Declaración de Cambio por Inversión Internacional) stamped by the authorized intermediary, original payout instruction, notarized corporate minutes, and certified share issuance ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent cash deposits above fingerprint limits and inconsistent POS settlement amounts in a supermarket retail model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Physical-store daily POS reconciliation, DIAN electronic invoicing with CUDE validation, cashier shift counts, insurance-policy cash-holding certificates, and monthly SARLAFT monitoring files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade settlement routed through third-party non-bank payment providers rather than the registered Colombian intermediary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier letter setting out irrevocable bank details, UCP600 credit terms, purchase order and LC draft, intermediary bank confirmation containing the channeling declaration, and a power of attorney appointing the local bank as the exclusive FX channel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident capital must be wired via SWIFT MT103 or equivalent from the shareholder’s bank to the local commercial bank’s foreign-currency account, with purpose code and reference text indicating ‘Aportes de Capital S.A.S. – Form No. 3 Foreign Investment’. The local bank will obtain the Banco de la República investment registration, validate the investor identity against the annual profit remittance records, credit the capital escrow account in USD or COP after BDC filing, and issue the formal channeling certificate to be attached to the statutory corporate books.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments to Asian condiment and grocery vendors shall be made through SWIFT MT103 under irrevocable documentary credits (UCP600) issued by the local bank, or under clean payment terms where the commercial invoice is authenticated by DIAN customs validation. For each disbursement the S.A.S. must present Form No. 2 (Importación de Bienes) to the intermediary, declare the exact purpose code, match the wire to B/L, invoice, and packing list, and preserve the bank certification of payment for tax and FX audits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore COP/USD Outright Forwards executed with an SFC-authorized commercial bank and tied to documented import/export exposure
COP/USD Non-Deliverable Forwards via authorized intermediaries where legal delivery of COP is avoided and settlement is made in USD pursuant to Banco de la República conditions
COP/USD Foreign Currency Swaps (FX Swaps) for rolling import settlement liquidity
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) limited to trade-finance debt and matching cash flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Mercantile Registration Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty equals up to 150% of the commercial registration fee and may trigger administrative strike-off of the registration if prolonged.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between April 5 and May 20 (specific date assigned by last two digits of NIT under DIAN annual calendar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of COP 500,000 to 1,500,000 per month of non-filing plus default interest and potential criminal prosecution for willful evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Filing after Shareholders' Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the shareholders' meeting, which must be held no later than March 31 following the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines imposed by the Chamber of Commerce and obstruction of sales to public entities or banks due to outdated filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Registry Update (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the annual filing period established by DIAN, typically running July to September
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines per non-compliant company, risk of being listed as prized/presumed evader, and suspension of administrative and commercial operations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Colombian SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) if it exceeds any one of the following: total assets above 5,000 monthly minimum legal wages (approx. USD 1.6 million), gross annual revenue above 3,000 monthly minimum legal wages (approx. USD 1.0 million), or 30 or more employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) for Group 2 entities (small and medium-sized enterprises) as issued by the Consejo Técnico de la Contaduría Pública (CTCP) under Law 1314 of 2009.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, the SAS must verify and confirm the identity of all ultimate beneficial owners as recorded in the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales). Any changes in shareholding, insider interest, or control structure must be filed with DIAN within the annual RUB window. The company must also certify in the shareholders' minute that the register is current.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas and Junta Directiva)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – USD 800 per year (varies by city and service quality)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 – USD 5,000 per year (depending on entity size and complexity of the IFRS for SME financial statements)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions: Colombia does not offer broad tax holidays for grocery retail; however, a 25% tax discount on investments in fixed real productive assets is available under Article 259-1 of the Colombian Tax Code (ET). Additionally, payroll deductions, parafiscal contributions, and depreciation of fixed assets may reduce effective liability. The presumptive income regime (renta presuntiva) may set a minimum taxable income equal to 3.5% of net equity when actual income is lower.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 110 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) filed electronically via DIAN’s Muisca portal (www.dian.gov.co) using a digital certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within the calendar year following the taxable year, generally between March and April depending on the last two digits of the NIT. The exact deadline is set by DIAN resolution each year. For a December 31 fiscal year-end, the filing deadline typically falls in mid-April. Quarterly prepayments are not applicable to ordinary S.A.S. entities unless income exceeds thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income from grocery sales, including debit and credit card receipts and cash sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Colombian-source income; non-resident owners must ensure that only the local S.A.S. reports sales income, not a foreign related entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income other than sales — e.g., recovered costs, reimbursements, or incidental income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any Colombian-source interest or rental income; do not net foreign expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments to gross income for prior-year differences and inflationary adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Follow Colombian inflation adjustment rules for fixed assets and inventory; no foreign inflators apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total costs of goods sold, including purchase price of imported Asian condiments, vegetables, and freight/customs duties capitalised into inventory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Costs must be supported by import documentation and may require transfer pricing adjustments if purchasing from a related non-resident supplier.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operational deductions: rent, salaries, utilities, freight, marketing, and depreciation of store fixtures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions require a causal link to Colombian income. Payments to non-resident related parties must meet arm's length standard and be supported by invoices and TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income after net operating losses and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute only after applying Colombian tax law adjustments; foreign tax credits are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax charge at the statutory rate (35%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The S.A.S. is the taxpayer; non-resident shareholders are not subject to CIT on the entity’s income unless deemed Colombian income arises.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: investment discount (Article 259-1 ET), taxes paid abroad (if applicable).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only credits specifically available to the entity can be applied; taxes withheld on dividends are a shareholder-level credit, not entity-level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance payable or balance to refund after prepayments and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the entity has excess withholding credits, request refund in the same filing where legally available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction of delay, up to a maximum of 100% of the tax due. If no tax is due, a fixed sanction of approximately COP 500,000 (equivalent to 10 UVT) applies. Monthly default interest on unpaid tax: 1.5%, increasing with the usury rate. Additional penalties for inaccuracy may be 20%-100% of the understated tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 7.5% (for dividends paid out of profits already taxed at 35% CIT to resident shareholders). For non-resident shareholders, the standard statutory dividend withholding tax rate is 10% on the gross dividend where the distributing company is not listed as a 'treaty-protected' entity; where the underlying profits were subject to the full 35% CIT, the additional 10% withholding applies, resulting in a combined statutory rate of 7.5% for resident individuals and 10% for non-residents. In specific cases, an extra 3% or 7.5% surtax may apply for excessive profits, but standard retail dividends attract the base rates.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced dividend withholding rate under a Colombia DTA, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the home-country tax authority (e.g., Form 6166 in the US, or equivalent). The TRC must be submitted to the Colombian paying S.A.S. before the dividend distribution, together with a completed Form 100 and Form 120 (or the simplified DIAN forms) for beneficial ownership declaration. The Colombian withholder must file the corresponding withholding declaration (Form 110 or separate Form 100 for withholdings) and retain the TRC for 5 years. The application must be made through the DIAN portal before the withholding event to apply the treaty rate; failure to do so results in 10% or 20% withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty withholding: 15% (Article 408 ET); reduced to 10% or 0% under certain DTAs (e.g., with US, Mexico, Spain, Chile). Statutory interest withholding: 15% for financial institutions, 20% for other lenders (or 15% under general rules); DTA rates for interest often 10% (e.g., with US, Netherlands, Spain, Switzerland). Payment must have economic substance, be documented, and comply with transfer pricing rules for related-party royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: COP 1,250,000,000 (approx. USD 300,000) in gross assets or gross income; or transactions with related parties exceeding COP 150,000,000 (approx. USD 36,000). When thresholds are exceeded, the taxpayer must prepare and file Local File, Master File and an annual Transfer Pricing Information Return (Form 120) with DIAN.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia’s tax framework requires economic substance under the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) and Article 122-1 ET. For an S.A.S. retailing imported products, substance is evidenced by physical store premises, operating payroll, inventory risk, and management decisions in Colombia. The entity must not be a mere conduit or pass-through for royalty or service fees; the OECD/G20 BEPS Action 6 principles and local case law require that the entity has the capability and actual exercise of control over its functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-declaring cash sales, manipulating inventory values, or using unregistered suppliers to reduce taxable income, or falsifying accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 4 to 9 years under Article 434A of the Criminal Code; fine up to COP 1,000,000,000 (approx. USD 250,000); tax exclusion and forfeiture of goods; civil restitution equal to the evaded tax plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable under the doctrine of veil-piercing when acting in bad faith; they face joint and several liability for tax debts and criminal imprisonment, travel bans, and asset freezes for the duration of proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing the S.A.S. without real activity, using it solely to channel profits abroad, or maintaining it with no employees, no physical store, or no actual importation despite claiming retail operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may disallow advantages, apply the GAAR, and assess tax on a presumptive basis; fines for defamation of tax advantage and potential money laundering charges under Law 1121/2006.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Shares may be ignored, and directors become personally liable for the company’s debts and taxes; travel bans and refusal to renew RUT may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained cash deposits, failing to maintain records of customers, or facilitating international trade payments through unofficial channels to avoid banking oversight.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering offenses are punishable under Law 1762/2015 with imprisonment of 10 to 30 years; assets may be forfeited; fines up to 50% of the laundered amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors must file Suspicious Transaction Reports (ROS) with the Financial Information Unit (UIAF); failure exposes them to criminal liability, personal fines, and prohibition from holding office in financial or commercial entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the grocery store without the required municipal commercial license (Registro Nacional de Turismo or local approval), or failing to collect and remit local consumption taxes (ICA/industry and commerce tax).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Closure of the establishment by the mayor; fines of up to 2,000 UVT for failure to remit ICA; arrest of responsible parties for up to 5 years under certain public order rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives of the S.A.S. are directly liable for unpaid ICA taxes and penalties; in case of closure, they may be suspended from re-entry to the municipality and face administrative fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file Form 120, Local File, or Master File when the entity’s transactions with non-resident related parties exceed the threshold; or not applying arm's length pricing on purchases from an overseas parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic increase in taxable income by 10% of transaction value (or higher at DIAN’s discretion); penalty of 200% of the omitted tax for non-compliance; daily fine of up to 50 UVT for each day of delay; formal penalty up to COP 1,000,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the return remain liable for adjustments; failure to produce documentation may lead to criminal investigation for false documentation; personal insolvency proceedings may follow if assessed penalty cannot be paid by the company.
